intent: Review only the completed curve-extraction support unit for ROUND-4 C2: read the existing Infineon PDF diagrams into typical Vf at25/125C and Eoss curves with reproducible provenance and explicit domains. A/C1/D1/C2/D2 execution is still in progress and outside this four-file review. Wrong curve identity, axis mapping or interpolation coverage can silently bias the eventual loss comparison; no hardware approval is intended.

findings.title: Grid-stroke centering shifts the voltage axis and low-bus Eoss readings
findings.suggested_fix: Calibrate X0 from the PDF numeric tick-label centers (80.8706pt at0V and296.9291pt at500V), verify the curve origin independently, and regenerate the CSV/provenance. Preserve the existing typical-value caveats.
findings.why_it_matters: The current origin shifts each Eoss query by0.463V. At10V the committed table says3.8686uJ instead of3.6230uJ from the actual tick-calibrated line, a6.8% error larger than the quoted0.2uJ graph-reading scale.
evidence: PDF page10 tick0 spans78.6466..83.0946pt, center80.8706; tick500 spans290.2571..303.6011pt, center296.9291.
In-memory intersections of the same582 line segments at10V: current origin3.868614uJ; tick-centered origin3.622990uJ. At1V the discrepancy is0.142722 versus0.069647uJ.
The separate400V Co(er) calibration still passes under both origins, so it does not detect this low-voltage axis bias.
